description:
## What breaks

A `"""` heredoc compiles and answers `""`. The content is dropped with no diagnostic, on every door.

```
fn main() do
  a = """
hello
"""
  dbg(a)
  dbg(Kernel.byte_size(a))
end
```

`interp`, `run` and `build` all print `""` and `0`.

## Why

The lexer has no heredoc concept. `src/parser/lexer.rs` dispatches on a single `b'"'` into `read_quoted_binary_parts`, which reads to the next `"`. Nothing anywhere looks ahead for a second or third quote.

So `"""` is not a delimiter -- it is an empty string followed by an opening quote. The program above lexes as `a = ""`, then a string holding `"\nhello\n"`, then another `""`. `a` gets the empty one.

`"""X"""` on a single line behaves identically to `"" "X" ""`, and both print `""`. That is the proof: there is no heredoc, only three quote characters.

The silence comes from juxtaposition being legal (fz-5xp.86): the parser accepts the trailing expressions and discards them.

## What to build

Heredoc lexing, matching Elixir's rules:

- `"""` opens a heredoc only when the rest of that line is blank; content starts on the next line.
- The closing `"""` sits on its own line, and its indentation is stripped from every content line.
- The result keeps each content line's newline and excludes the closing delimiter's line, so `"""\nhello\n"""` is `"hello\n"`.
- Escapes and `#{}` interpolation work inside, as they do in a single-quoted string -- the lexer already has `StringPart` and `read_interpolation_range` for that.

## Acceptance

- A heredoc lexes to one binary token carrying its content.
- Indentation is stripped relative to the closing delimiter.
- Interpolation inside a heredoc reaches `Kernel.to_string/1` the way it does in a regular string.
- The ordinary string consumers receive the heredoc as one whole value. In particular, `@doc` and `@moduledoc` preserve paragraphs, blank lines and example indentation through their distinct quoted-surface paths.
- Focused lexer and quoted-surface tests plus a fixture prove content and byte size on all four paths.

comments.text: Done in 5d7fa2ebb. Heredoc lexing with Elixir's rules: opening line refuses content, closing line's indentation stripped from each content line, content lines keep their newlines, escapes and interpolation work. De-indenting happens in place so interpolation ranges still point into the original source. Five lexer tests plus a behaviour fixture whose Elixir twin agrees byte for byte. An outdented line strips what it has (Elixir's value) without Elixir's warning; the lexer has no telemetry to warn through.

title: [BUG] fz has no heredoc syntax, and `"""` silently lexes as adjacent string literals
